data. Thus from south to north, interpreted ages span the Upper Aalenian–Middle Bathonian through the
Callovian. Therefore, magnetostratigraphy was used to better precise the age of the Formation at Portada

itisinterpretedthatthestudiedsectionwasnotsubjectedtorotationsaroundverticalaxis(R=4°±10°),but
wascompacted,whichproducedinclinationshallowingofthemagneticvector(F=18°±11°).Thecalculated
inclinationshallowingandamountofcompactioninthesectionarewellwithintheexpectedvaluesinmedium
to fine-grained sandstones. Using the paleomagnetic pole from Mamil Choique as reference, the locality of
PortadaCovuncowouldhavebeenlocatedatc.33°SduringtheBathonian,inagreementwithpaleoclimatic
interpretationsderivedfrompalynologicaldata.

Paleomagnetic treatment involved both alternating field (AF) and
thermal(TH)demagnetizationmethods,carriedoutattheLaboratório
de Paleomagnetismo do Departamento de Geofísica – Instituto de As-
tronomia,GeofísicaeCiênciasAtmosféricas,UniversidaddeSaoPaulo,
Brasil.Fordemagnetizationtreatments,aTD48Schoenstedovenanda
2GAFdemagnetizerwereused.Residualremanentmagnetizationwas
measuredwithacryogenic2GDCSQUIDmagnetometer.
Anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) and rock magnetic
studies were performed at the Laboratorio D. Valencio, IGEBA. For
AMS, measurements were performed with an AGICO MFK1A
Kappabridge equipped with an automatic spinner that produces 64
measurements on each of the three axes of the specimen. For rock
magneticstudies,isothermalremanentmagnetization(IRM)acquisition
and thermomagnetic (bulk susceptibility versus temperature) curves
wereobtained.ForIRMacquisitioncurves,samplesfromrepresentative
lithologies were subjected to a 13 steps sequence, using an IM-10-30
pulsemagnetizer(ASCScientific)to1T.Aftereachstep,theremanence
was measured with aJR6 Dual Speed Spinner Magnetometer (AGICO
inc.).ThermomagneticcurveswereperformedinAratmospheremea-
sured in representative specimens using the AGICO MFK1-FA Multi-
Function Kappabridge coupled to high-temperature (CS4) and low- temperature(CSL)controllers.Theamplitudeoftheappliedalternating
fieldwas200A/m,atafrequencyof997Hz.Atlowtemperaturesthe
rangecoveredwasfrom−188°Cto5°Candathightemperaturesfrom
30°Cupto680°C.
5. Anisotropyofmagneticsusceptibility
AMS studies the petrofabrics of rocks, and depends on the aniso-
tropy of individual grains and their spatial arrangement in a rock.
Magnetic properties vary with the direction, determining different
types of anisotropy (Borradaile and Henry, 1997a,b; Borradaile and
Jackson,1993;LanzaandMeloni,2006).AMSdatarecordthepreferred
orientation of anisotropic magnetic minerals, i.e. paramagnetic, dia-
magnetic and ferromagnetic minerals that make up the rock. The

11. Conclusions
ThestudiedsectionoftheLajasFormationcroppingoutatPortada
Covuncoisa290m-thicksuccessionmadeupofconglomerates,sand-
stones and mudstones that reaches. Two facies associations were de-
finedwithin afluvial-dominated delta system:facies association 1 in-
terpreted as progradation of mouth bars in a delta front setting, and
faciesassociation2ashyperpycnalprodeltalobes.
The isolated characteristic remanent magnetization passed the re-
versaltestasRc(McFaddenandMcElhinny,1990),indicatingthatno
systematic secondary components biased the remanence directions.
Furthermore, since normal and reverse directions belong to the same
stratigraphic section, they most likely represent the primary magneti-
zation. Based on rock magnetic and paleomagnetic studies, this com-
ponent would be carried primarily, by PSD titanium-poor magnetite
andpossiblyhematite.Asystematicsecondarymagneticcomponentis
interpreted as representing either remagnetization produced by the
present-day magnetic field on MD or large PSD grains or, a chemical
remagnetization acquired during the first stages of formation of the
Agriofoldandthrustbeltduetofluidsmigration.

direction of 73° (NE) and angular deviation of 39°. Such lineation of
K axesdoesnotrelatewiththemaximumstressσ directionrevealed
max 1
by the regional NW-SE fold axis. Instead the clustering of the K
max

faceofcurrentripplesaligningthefabricswiththeflowwhichinthis
case are directed to the NE (Felletti et al., 2016), in agreement with
paleocurrentsmeasuredintheregionfromsedimentarystructures.
